speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder; let's start by describing exactly what you are seeing in your movements, such as tremors, rigidity, or involuntary jerking.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the update. The significant improvement in your psychiatric symptoms is good to hear. To investigate the new onset movement disorder, can you tell me exactly how your movements feel and if you notice any stiffness or shaking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced Acute Dystonic Reaction / Tardive Dyskinesia (likely Akathisia given the restlessness and pacing). 

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain to rule out other structural causes for the movement disorder.

Please confirm if you feel an inner restlessness that makes it difficult to sit still, and check if you have any muscle spasms or pain in your neck or jaw.
